Conversation, family & daily routines

any news? phrase

also news, what’s new?, is there any news?, no other news, I’ll tell you when I have any news, if you have any news, nothing new

classical

Plin. Ep. 3.14.6: quid praetereā novī? Nihil (Lewis & Short s.v. subjungō)
Traupman 104: is there any news?, num quid novī?

Quid novī?

quid with the partitive genitive novī, “what of new?”

what’s new? any news?

News in Latin is “something new”: aliquid novī, nihil novī, with the neuter genitive. The noun “news”, a report of events, is nūntius.

Other words

  • Numquid novī? — is there any news?

    also used · Renaissance · Erasmus, Colloquia, Nova rogandī I 58–59: Num quid novī? (loci collection; post-classical); Franmorarius, Dē variīs fōrmulīs XXV.2 (loci collection; modern); Traupman 104: is there any news?, num quid novī?

    Numquid expects the answer no or leaves it open: “there isn’t any news, is there?” Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

Examples

  • nihil novī ad nōs adferēbātur

    no news was reaching usCic. Fam. 2.14 (Lewis & Short s.v. afferō)

  • Sī quid forte novī habēs dē eā rē …

    If you happen to have any news about it …Traupman 104

  • Narrābō, cum aliquid habēbō novī.

    I’ll tell you when I have any news.Traupman 104

  • Nihil praetereā novī.

    No other news.Traupman 104

See also newspaper.
